subject: Request: One-time transitional credit for BetaHealth due to delayed low-latency rollout
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: one-time transitional credit for BetaHealth (delayed low-latency rollout)

Team —

Short version: BetaHealth is asking for a one-time credit to offset the impact of our delayed low-latency streaming feature that they baked into their Q3 pilot. They are at risk of pausing expansion unless we offer a commercial accommodation while the feature ships (ETA early Aug).

Context:
- BetaHealth (enterprise pilot) integrated our streaming SDK expecting the low-latency commit we planned for June. That optimization slipped to late July / early Aug due to a kernel scheduling regression discovered during internal perf tests.
- They experienced increased CPU usage and higher token costs in their pilot environment, which pushed their projected POC economics out by ~3 weeks. Usage report attached.

Customer ask: one-time transitional credit (we proposed $18k) to cover incremental token/GPU delta while they complete validation. They are asking for exec sign-off because their procurement requires written confirmation.

Requested from you:
1) Aditya — commercial approval to offer $18k one-time credit tied to the deal BH-2027-0421. Confirm whether this sits inside existing discount authority or needs VP sign-off.
2) Marcus — approx finance impact and any GL restrictions we need to note (recognition timing, refund vs credit).
3) Laura — what can product promise re: timeline and rollback risk? Is early-Aug still realistic and do we have a mitigation (prefetch/batching) to suggest as short-term recommendation to the customer?

Attachments: betahealth_q2_usage_summary.csv, proposed_transitional_credit.xlsx, impact_note_betahealth.pdf

I think a narrow, one-off credit tied to the rollout milestone (credit expires if feature delivery slips past Aug 15) is reasonable and preserves precedent. Will loop in legal if this needs special contracting language.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

--
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: one-time transitional credit for BetaHealth (delayed low-latency rollout)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. I support offering a one-time, conditional credit in principle. A few quick asks before I escalate to Jaya (VP Sales):
- Confirm how the $18k was calculated (is that incremental cost for the 3-week delta or includes downstream integration support?). I see the usage CSV but want a simple line-item.
- Make the credit contingent on an agreed milestone: delivery of low-latency v1 (release tag + date) or automatic expiration Aug 15 as you suggested.
- Please confirm whether BetaHealth has an outstanding credit request in the last 12 months — we should avoid stacking.

If those are clear, I will seek VP approval today. Marcus — any showstopper from finance?

- Aditya

Vanessa / Aditya —

Reviewed the numbers. Finance is okay with a one-time credit up to $20k gross, provided these conditions are met:
1) Credit is issued as an account credit (applied to next invoice) rather than a cash refund.
2) Credit must be milestone-gated: release tag + QA validation or auto-expire Aug 15, 2027.
3) We need an internal memo (1-paragraph) that documents the reason code and impacted GL for audit (I can draft).
4) No stacking: confirm BetaHealth has no other active commercial accommodations in the past 12 months.

If Aditya gets VP nod, finance will prep the accounting memo and approve GL posting.

Marcus

Hi Vanessa / Aditya —

Thanks for the prompt follow-up and for being transparent about the delay. We appreciate Redwood’s proposal for a limited credit while we finish performance validation on our end. A few clarifications from procurement:
- Confirmation that the credit is account-applied (we prefer that) and will appear on our next invoice.
- We agree to milestone gating: we will accept the credit subject to Redwood delivering the stated low-latency release and passing the acceptance tests we agreed to in the POC checklist.
- Please provide a short written acknowledgement (one paragraph) that the credit is a one-time accommodation and does not change the rest of the commercial terms.

If you can send the acknowledgement and credit schedule today, our procurement team will sign off quickly.

Best,
